[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Federated teams applying policy, tone, and taxonomy rules independently produce outputs with divergent policy application and fragmented user experience. When policy requirements change, updates must be applied to every team's local implementation rather than to a single controlled location.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Centralize cross-cutting controls — policy directives, controlled vocabulary, provenance rules, and naming and formatting conventions — in a shared instruction set that all agents reference, rather than allowing each team to implement local copies.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Any agent that operates in a compliance-relevant context where policy consistency is required
- When multiple agents in the same portfolio must apply the same policy directive or provenance labeling convention
- When a policy requirement changes and must be applied consistently across all capabilities immediately
page_texts.7:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Policy updates are applied once in the shared instruction set and immediately effective across all capabilities that reference it
- Eliminates inconsistency in policy application between agent teams
- Makes policy exceptions visible — because they must be explicitly documented rather than quietly omitted from a local copy
page_texts.9:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

A federated delivery model enables team autonomy. That autonomy extends to the policy and tone instructions in agent prompts unless a shared instruction set creates a consistency constraint. Policy directives applied locally by each team diverge over time through independent prompt edits, team turnover, and different interpretations of the same underlying policy.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

For configured agents on the M365 Copilot platform, instructions can be maintained in a shared instruction set and referenced by multiple agents. For custom agents, shared policy directives can be implemented as a shared prompt module imported by the agent's code. In both cases, the technical constraint is that local copies of policy instructions are not permitted in Production state.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without centralized guardrails, the following failure modes are observed:
- Policy directives are copied from one agent's prompt to another, creating a point-in-time fork. When the policy is updated, the update is not propagated to all copies.
- Each team uses its own terminology for shared concepts — creating outputs that are structurally incompatible with each other even when they address the same workflow
- Provenance labeling (identifying the evidence source for each output element) is applied inconsistently, undermining audit confidence
page_texts.12:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Teams may resist depending on a centralized instruction set they do not control
- The shared instruction set must be maintained under change control, which adds governance overhead compared to local team ownership
- Changes to the shared instruction set affect all agents that reference it — the change control tier for shared policy instructions is the highest (Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board approval per STD-TEC-AI-004)
page_texts.14:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Maintain all cross-cutting controls in a centralized shared instruction set. Each capability's prompt references this shared instruction set rather than including a local copy. The four categories of cross-cutting controls that belong in the shared instruction set are:

1. **Policy directives** — compliance controls, prohibited content patterns, mandatory disclaimers, tone requirements that apply across all capabilities
2. **Controlled vocabulary** — the canonical terminology for shared concepts; eliminates synonyms and homonyms that produce inconsistent outputs
3. **Provenance rules** — the required labeling format for identifying evidence sources in outputs; ensures audit traceability
4. **Naming and formatting conventions** — the required format for output artifacts; ensures structural consistency across teams

Local prompt forks of shared instructions are not permitted in Production state. If a capability genuinely requires an exception to a shared instruction, the exception must be documented and approved per the exceptions process in STD-TEC-AI-004.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CC[Change Control\nEnterprise Architecture Board\nHighest Approval Tier] --> SI
    SI[Shared Instruction Set\nPolicy Directives\nControlled Vocabulary\nProvenance Rules\nFormatting Conventions]
    SI --> A[Agent A Prompt]
    SI --> B[Agent B Prompt]
    SI --> C[Agent N Prompt]
    ER[Exception Register\nDocumented + Approved] -.->|Approved fork only| A
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Shared instruction set | Maintains canonical cross-cutting controls | STD-TEC-AI-004 (centralization requirement) |
| Capability prompt | References the shared instruction set; adds capability-specific instructions | STD-TEC-AI-004 |
| Change control process | Governs changes to the shared instruction set | STD-GOV-AI-004 |
| Exception register | Records approved exceptions to shared instructions | STD-TEC-AI-004 exceptions process |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Cross-cutting policy, vocabulary, provenance, and formatting requirements are identified and documented in the shared instruction set
2. Each capability's prompt references the shared instruction set for all cross-cutting controls
3. When a policy requirement changes, the change is made to the shared instruction set under the Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board change control tier, versioned, and validated against the regression scenario suite (per STD-TEC-AI-005) for a representative sample of referencing capabilities before rollout
4. Each capability that references the shared instruction set is promoted to the new version per its own change record and rollback plan (per STD-GOV-AI-004) rather than receiving the change silently; capabilities are not required to adopt the new version simultaneously
5. Exceptions require explicit approval and documentation in the exception register
page_texts.18:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Layered guardrails**: A shared enterprise instruction set supplemented by a domain-level instruction set — capabilities reference both layers. Domain-level guardrails may not override enterprise-level guardrails.
- **Policy module per compliance domain**: Separate shared instruction sets for different compliance domains (e.g., data privacy, clinical content, financial output) that are referenced selectively by relevant capabilities
page_texts.20:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Shared instruction set storage location defined and accessible to the Platform Governance Team
- All cross-cutting policy requirements documented and reviewed before the shared instruction set is published
- Change control tier for shared instruction set changes understood by all domain owners
page_texts.22:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#phase-1-shared-instruction-set-authoring]

#### Phase 1: Shared Instruction Set Authoring

1. Identify all cross-cutting controls currently implemented locally across existing capabilities
2. Draft the canonical version of each control — resolving inconsistencies between team-local implementations
3. Organize controls into the four categories (policy directives, controlled vocabulary, provenance rules, naming and formatting conventions)
4. Review the draft shared instruction set with the Platform Governance Team and Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board before publishing
page_texts.23:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#phase-2-capability-integration]

#### Phase 2: Capability Integration

1. For each existing capability: identify where local copies of shared instructions exist in the capability's prompts
2. Replace local copies with a reference to the shared instruction set
3. Test the capability against the quality rubric after the replacement to confirm no behavioral regression
page_texts.24:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#phase-3-change-governance]

#### Phase 3: Change Governance

1. All subsequent changes to the shared instruction set follow the policy and governance change control tier per STD-GOV-AI-004 and STD-TEC-AI-004
2. Conduct quarterly review of the shared instruction set to confirm it remains aligned with current policy requirements
page_texts.25:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Publish the shared instruction set before any capability enters Pilot state — retrofitting centralization into Production capabilities is a higher-risk change than designing for it from the start
- Define the controlled vocabulary in consultation with domain owners — enforcing terminology that domain teams do not use creates friction rather than consistency
- When a policy change requires an urgent update to the shared instruction set, use the emergency change process per STD-GOV-AI-004 with documented rollback readiness
page_texts.26:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- Allowing "minor" local overrides of shared instructions that gradually expand in scope until the local copy diverges significantly from the canonical version
- Failing to test all capabilities that reference the shared instruction set after a policy update — the shared instruction set is a dependency for every agent that references it
- Publishing a shared instruction set without a defined change control process — without governance, the shared instruction set will drift through ad hoc edits

### Compliance Requirements

- Local prompt forks of shared policy instructions in Production state require architecture board approval
- Changes to the shared instruction set require Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board approval
page_texts.30:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

- Shared instruction set publication requires Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board review
- Policy changes within the shared instruction set follow the policy and governance change control tier (highest tier) per STD-GOV-AI-004
page_texts.31:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| Policy compliance incident count | Declining over time | Per STD-TEC-AI-006 metric collection |
| Cross-team output taxonomy variance | Low and declining | Monthly portfolio hygiene review |
| Local policy fork exceptions in Production | Zero without documented approval | Monthly prompt library audit per STD-TEC-AI-004 |
page_texts.34:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#scenario-1-policy-update-propagation]

#### Scenario 1: Policy update propagation

The enterprise adds a new required disclaimer for all AI-generated content. The shared instruction set is updated once with the new disclaimer text, under the policy and governance change control tier. All capabilities referencing the shared instruction set receive the update without per-team action.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#scenario-2-controlled-vocabulary-alignment]

#### Scenario 2: Controlled vocabulary alignment

Two domain teams use different terms for the same concept in their agent outputs, creating downstream confusion in workflow handoffs. The shared instruction set is updated to define the canonical term, and both teams update their prompts to reference the centralized definition.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

Each team maintains local copies of policy instructions in their prompts. Policy updates require coordinated action across all teams. Teams drift from each other's implementations over time through independent edits.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

All cross-cutting policy, vocabulary, provenance, and formatting requirements are maintained in a shared instruction set. Capabilities reference the shared set. Policy updates take effect immediately across all capabilities.

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-010-shared-guardrail-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Federated teams implement cross-cutting policy, vocabulary, and provenance rules locally, creating inconsistency that is expensive to synchronize when policy changes.

**Solution:** Centralize all cross-cutting controls in a shared instruction set referenced by all capabilities; prohibit local forks in Production state.

**When to Use:** Any agent operating in a compliance-relevant context; any portfolio where multiple agents must apply the same policy or terminology consistently.

**Key Benefits:**
- Policy updates applied once, effective everywhere
- Eliminates inter-team policy divergence
- Makes exceptions visible and auditable

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** Shared instruction set storage, change control tier understood, existing cross-cutting controls identified

**Related Patterns:** PTN-TEC-AI-009 Contract-First Agent, PTN-GOV-AI-012 Federated Change Gateway
